page: Microsoft Azure E192ds_v7 is a memory-optimized server instance belonging to the Edsv7 family, built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated virtual CPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. This hardware configuration provides 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled and a total of 1536.0 GB of system memory, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes a substantial 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for vector and matrix operations. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 11339 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with both small-block cached read-only speeds and large-block uncached read and write speeds ranking in the top 10%. Single-core performance, however, is moderate, with stress-ng single-core benchmarks falling into the middle 50%. This performance profile translates to highly efficient parallel processing but highlights a tradeoff where single-threaded tasks do not see the same relative performance advantages. In LLM inference tests, the server demonstrates strong prompt processing capabilities, but text generation speeds are comparatively limited, falling into the average or weak categories depending on the model size.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and massive local storage capacity, the E192ds_v7 is designed for memory-intensive and data-heavy workloads. It achieves top-tier results in database operations and Redis SET benchmarks, making it suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching layers, and complex data warehousing. The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is characterized by its high resource density, combining massive memory capacity with high-speed local storage on a single dedicated host. This reduces the need for multi-node clustering for large datasets, though the lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training workloads.
